title: Characterization of sorting order
statement: Let $k:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$, and let $N,i,j\in\mathbb{N}$ with $i<N$ and $j<N$. The position of $i$ in the ordering of the first $N$ indices by increasing $k$-value, with ties broken by increasing index, is strictly less than the position of $j$ if and only if either $k(i)<k(j)$, or $k(i)=k(j)$ and $i<j$.
hypotheses_covered: $k$ is a function from natural numbers to natural numbers.
